ceiling_directive: Prove a class-transfer theorem deriving the asymmetric polyhedral endpoint game from the published directional-derivative limit-experiment primitives, and instantiate the no-index result within that transferred class rather than only on the note's constructed game class.
improvement_directive: Resolve `oeq:unbalanced-no-index-witness` affirmatively by giving explicit rational game and unequal-sign prior data, together with outward-rounded interval and tail bounds proving exact primal-dual closure and nonvanishing curvature. This would turn the conditional geometric implication into an actual no-one-index result on the same estimand.
critique: The note does not deliver the advertised all-one-index, coexistence, or no-one-index classification: `oeq:indexability-criterion` remains open. Its no-one-index theorem is only an implication whose premises require exact saddle closure and a curved score-zero arc, while `oeq:unbalanced-no-index-witness` leaves open whether any qualifying asymmetric game and prior exist. What is concretely established is compact-game saddle duality, convergence of an exact-oracle exchange scheme without a complexity guarantee, and a triangular coexistence example that still has a constant one-index optimum. The feasible transfer additionally assumes strong two-sided and joint total-variation approximations and does not prove measurable dependence of the selected near-saddle rule on the randomly estimated game. Thus the framing's "theorem-level frontier" is a conditional diagnostic, not a realized no-one-index frontier or the promised correspondence classification.
